questions.question: Which of the following dances developed in the monasteries of Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form that originated in the **monasteries of Assam**.
 
• It was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint **Sankardeva** in the 15th century as a medium for religious expression and storytelling.
 
• The dance form is an integral part of the **Sattras (monastic institutions)** and was traditionally performed by male monks known as **Bhakats**.
 
• **Sattriya** dance includes various elements such as **nritta (pure dance), nritya (expressive dance), and natya (dramatic elements)**.
 
• In 2000, **Sattriya** was recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya** dance is characterized by its use of **hand gestures (mudras), footwork (padas), and facial expressions (abhinaya)**.
 
• The costumes typically include traditional Assamese attire with elaborate jewelry and headgear.
 
• Music accompanying **Sattriya** dance is based on classical ragas and is performed using traditional instruments like the **khol (drum), taals (cymbals), and flute**.
 
• Over time, **Sattriya** has evolved and is now performed by both men and women on various cultural platforms.

questions.question: Which power were the Badami (or Vatapi) Chalukyas originally subjects of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kadambas**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kadambas** were the original power to whom the **Badami (or Vatapi) Chalukyas** were subjects.
 
• The Kadambas ruled from Banavasi in present-day Karnataka, and their reign is considered significant in the early medieval history of the Deccan region.
 
• The Chalukyas later rose to prominence and established their own dynasty, with Badami (Vatapi) as their capital.
 
• The Chalukyas are well-known for their contributions to art and architecture, particularly in the construction of rock-cut temples.
 
• The transition from being subjects of the Kadambas to establishing their own rule marks a significant period in South Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Badami Chalukyas** ruled from the** 6th to the 8th century CE** and are known for their architectural innovations and military prowess.
 
• Their capital, Badami, is famous for its cave temples, which are exemplary specimens of Indian rock-cut architecture.
 
• The Chalukyas fought several wars with neighboring dynasties such as the **Pallavas and the Rashtrakutas**, which shaped the political landscape of the region.
 
• The Kadambas, on the other hand, are one of the earliest native dynasties to rule over Karnataka and are credited with laying the foundation for the later development of Kannada literature and culture.
 
• The period of **Chalukya rule** is often regarded as a g**olden age in the history of Karnataka**, characterized by economic prosperity and cultural achievements.

questions.question: Mohammad Yunus established which of the following banks in 1983?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grameen Bank**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Grameen Bank** was established by **Mohammad Yunus in 1983**.
 
• It is a microfinance organization and community development bank founded in **Bangladesh**.
 
• Grameen Bank makes **small loans (known as microcredit or "Grameencredit")** to the impoverished without requiring collateral.
 
• The bank and its founder, Mohammad Yunus, were awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize in 2006** for their efforts to create economic and social development from below.
 
• The model of microfinance pioneered by Grameen Bank has been replicated in many countries around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Microfinance** is a type of **banking service** that is **provided to unemployed or low-income individuals or groups** who otherwise would have no other access to financial services.
 
• Microfinance allows people to take on reasonable small business loans safely, and in a manner that is consistent with ethical lending practices.
 
• Grameen Bank's approach is based on the idea that the poor have skills that are underutilized and that financial capital can help them to leverage these skills to improve their economic conditions.
 
• Mohammad Yunus's vision was to eradicate poverty through entrepreneurship and self-sustaining business practices among the poor.

questions.question: When was the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) launched by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1999**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)** was launched by the Government of India in **1999**.
 
• The scheme aimed to bring the assisted poor families (Swarozgaris) above the poverty line by organizing them into **Self Help Groups (SHGs)** through a mix of bank credit and government subsidy.
 
• It focused on promoting **self-employment in rural areas** through the establishment of **micro-enterprises**.
 
• SGSY was a major anti-poverty scheme that targeted the rural poor, particularly women and vulnerable sections of society.
 
• The scheme was later restructured as the **National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) in 2011** to further strengthen the self-employment approach.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The SGSY scheme was implemented by the **Ministry of Rural Development**.
 
• It sought to provide sustainable income to the rural poor through a combination of economic activities, infrastructure support, and capacity building.
 
• Under the SGSY, assistance was provided to SHGs for the purchase of assets and skill development training.
 
• The scheme also emphasized the importance of marketing support and technology upgradation for the products produced by SHGs.
 
• SGSY was one of the flagship programs of the Indian government to **alleviate rural poverty and promote inclusive growth**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about the Five-Year Plan?

options.text: All Five-Year Plans have equal rates of growth.
The Planning Commission was constituted in 1951.
The President was the ex-officio chairperson of the Planning Commission.
The first Five-Year Plan was started in 1951.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the first Five-Year Plan was started in 1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first Five-Year Plan** was started in **1951**.
 
• The Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs initiated by the Government of India.
 
• The primary aim was to achieve specific economic goals and promote balanced growth.
 
• The **Planning Commission, established in 1950**, was responsible for formulating these plans.
 
• While the first Five-Year Plan focused on agricultural development, subsequent plans targeted various sectors such as industry, education, and health.
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog in 2015**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Planning Commission** was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India’s Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• It was established in **1950** by a resolution of the Government of India.
 
• The **Prime Minister** of India was the** ex-officio chairperson of the Planning Commission**.
 
• The Five-Year Plans were** inspired by the Soviet model** of economic planning and emphasized public sector development.
 
• With the dissolution of the Planning Commission, the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) was formed to replace it, aiming for a more bottom-up approach to economic planning and development.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stringed instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flute**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flute** is a **woodwind instrument**, not a stringed instrument.
 
• Stringed instruments produce sound through the vibration of strings. Examples include the **Guitar, Violin, and Mandolin**.
 
• The **Flute** produces sound when air is blown across the opening, causing the air within the instrument to vibrate.
 
• Stringed instruments typically have strings made of materials such as nylon, steel, or gut, which are plucked, strummed, or played with a bow.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Guitar** is a popular stringed instrument used in various music genres including rock, jazz, and classical.
 
• The **Violin** is a high-pitched stringed instrument often used in classical music and orchestras.
 
• The **Mandolin** is a stringed instrument with a distinct, bright sound, commonly used in folk and bluegrass music.
 
• Woodwind instruments, like the **Flute**, do not have strings and are played by blowing air into or across an opening.

questions.question: According to Global Multidimensional poverty index (2022), which of the following groups of states is included in top 10 poorest states of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya and Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya and Madhya Pradesh** are included in the **top 10 poorest states of India** according to the **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (2022)**.
 
• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) assesses poverty at the individual level by considering various deprivations people face in their daily lives, such as **health, education, and living standards**.
 
• States like Meghalaya and Madhya Pradesh have shown significant levels of poverty in multiple dimensions, contributing to their ranking in the top 10 poorest states of India.
 
• The MPI is a valuable tool for understanding the complexity of poverty and for shaping policies aimed at poverty alleviation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)** is developed by the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**.
 
• The MPI complements traditional income-based measures of poverty by considering overlapping deprivations in health, education, and living standards.
 
• India has made significant progress in reducing poverty, but regional disparities remain, with some states still facing high levels of multidimensional poverty.
 
• Addressing multidimensional poverty requires targeted interventions in areas such as healthcare, education, sanitation, and housing.
 
• The MPI can help policymakers identify priority areas for investment and track the effectiveness of poverty reduction strategies over time.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution is described as the ‘Magna Carta of India’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part III**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part III** of the Indian Constitution is described as the '**Magna Carta of India**'.
 
• It contains the **Fundamental Rights** that are guaranteed to all citizens of India, ensuring civil liberties and protection under the law.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the overall development of individuals and for maintaining a democratic framework.
 
• The Fundamental Rights include the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
 
• Part III of the Constitution aims to protect individuals from any arbitrary actions by the state and to promote the principles of justice, liberty, and equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about eutrophication is correct?

options.text: It happens when too less nitrogen is present in the water, causing reduced growth of plants and algae.
It is a beneficial process for environment restoration.
It happens when too much nitrogen enriches the water, causing excessive growth of plants and algae.
It happens when too much carbon enriches the water, causing excessive growth of bacteria and reduced growth of plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It happens when too much nitrogen enriches the water, causing excessive growth of plants and algae.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is a process where water bodies become enriched with nutrients, particularly nitrogen and phosphorus.
 
• This nutrient enrichment leads to **excessive growth of algae and aquatic plants**, which can result in harmful algal blooms.
 
• These algal blooms can deplete oxygen levels in the water, causing **dead zones** where aquatic life cannot survive.
 
• The primary sources of nutrients causing eutrophication include agricultural runoff, wastewater discharge, and industrial effluents.
 
• Eutrophication can lead to a loss of biodiversity, changes in species composition and dominance, and overall deterioration of water quality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preventive measures** include reducing nutrient runoff through better agricultural practices, improving sewage treatment facilities, and implementing policies to control industrial discharges.
 
• Restoration efforts for eutrophic water bodies may involve **mechanical, chemical, or biological methods** to remove excess nutrients and restore ecological balance.
 
• Public awareness and education about the sources and impacts of eutrophication are crucial for long-term water quality management.
 
• International cooperation and regulations, such as the European Union's Water Framework Directive, play a vital role in addressing transboundary water pollution issues.

questions.question: On 26 January 1950 India became:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** a sovereign, democratic, republic state**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On **26 January 1950**, India officially became a **sovereign, democratic, republic state**.
 
• This date marks the adoption of the **Constitution of India**, which laid down the legal framework for the country.
 
• The Constitution was adopted by the **Constituent Assembly** on **26th November 1949** and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• It established India as a republic, meaning that the head of state is elected, not a hereditary monarch.
 
• It also declared India as a sovereign state, indicating its independence from any external control.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written constitution** in the world and provides for a democratic system of government.
 
• It assures its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity among them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India also declares the nation to be **socialist and secular**, terms that were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
 
• The Constitution outlines the fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and duties of citizens.
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List, delineating the subjects under which each level of government has legislative powers.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Constitution has been amended multiple times to address the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Nehru Institute of Mountaineering is located at ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nehru Institute of Mountaineering** is located in **Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand**.
 
• It was established in **1965** to honor the **memory of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru**, who was an ardent mountain lover.
 
• The institute offers various courses in mountaineering, including Basic, Advanced, and Method of Instruction courses, as well as specialized courses like Search and Rescue.
 
• It is one of the premier mountaineering institutes in India, along with the **Himalayan Mountaineering Institute in Darjeeling**.
 
• The institute aims to promote mountaineering as a sport and to inculcate the spirit of adventure among the youth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Uttarakhand, often referred to as the "**Land of the Gods**," is known for its natural beauty and is a popular destination for trekking and mountaineering.
 
• The state is home to several other important mountaineering and adventure sports institutes, including the** Indian Military Academy** in Dehradun.
 
• Uttarakhand is also famous for its pilgrimage sites, such as Haridwar, Rishikesh, and the Char Dham (Badrinath, Kedarnath, Gangotri, and Yamunotri).
